Jordan / team — I pulled a quick sensitivity sheet and dropped it into token-econ-sensitivity.csv (attached referenced in MAP workbook). Main takeaways:
- Tokens/$ baseline 45k (your hosted quoted number) assumes 8-bit quant + 90 token average. If median is 95 and 90th is 260, effective tokens/$ falls ~12–18% without batching improvements.
- Cache hit rate matters: moving from 35% -> 50% reduces token spend by ~9% for this workload. That's mostly from prefix caching for templated lookups.
- Batching window: many of Greenline's interactive flows need < 100ms tail latencies. We can safely batch non-interactive flows at 100–250ms windows to increase throughput. For interactive UI we suggest a 25ms batching target and prioritize those requests on low-latency hosts.
- Prefetch recommendation: for workflows that begin with a small deterministic set of follow-up calls (e.g., triage -> recommended content), prefetching the next prompt in background can raise tokens served by the cache/prefetch pipeline by ~6–8% and reduce end-to-end latency for users. Tradeoff is slightly higher overall token volume if the prefetched branch isn't used.

Actionable asks from my side:
1) Validate whether prefetching is acceptable for clinical flows (privacy + audit considerations) — Alex/procurement.
2) Confirm the split of interactive vs background flows (we need a route-level %).

Team — building an eval plan in the MAP to gate pilot acceptance. Draft plan below (will put into GLH_MAP_v1.xlsx -> tab "eval_plan"):

Evaluation plan (2-week pilot):
- Week 0: Baseline measurement on 1000 sessions using current traffic replay to measure median/90th seq lengths and cache eligibility.
- Weeks 1–2: Run production-like traffic split (10% traffic) with Redwood in hosted dedicated pilot cluster. Measure: tokens consumed, effective tokens/$, p95/p99 latencies, cache hit rate, and user-visible error rate.

Gating thresholds (pass/fail):
- Cost gate: effective tokens/$ must be >= 32k (if lower, trigger batching+prefetch runbook and 1-week mitigation window).
- Latency gate: p95 < 500ms, p99 < 1.5s. If latency exceeds, increase low-latency capacity or reduce batching for interactive routes.
- Quality gate: automated eval set (N=500 prompts) must have generation pass-rate >= 92% on clinical fidelity checks.

If a gate fails, the MAP includes two mitigations: (A) prioritize caching and prefetch optimizations (track delta); (B) model variant fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant with documented quality delta (we'll document tradeoffs in the MAP).

I will attach token-econ-sensitivity.csv with the scenarios. Ben — flag anything I missed w.r.t. achievable batching windows on-host.
